compareDisposition.rationale: The curator examined Moses flees while Israel cries out beside Israel multiplies in Egypt; Egypt oppresses Israel; Moses is drawn from the Nile. Those passages share its exodus evidence group or Scripture movement, but none supplies a distinct two-source relationship stronger than the accepted comparisons already carrying this topic.

context.body: The remembered covenant is named with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
context.label: Covenant names

observations.body: Moses sees an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, kills the Egyptian, hides him, becomes afraid, and flees from Pharaoh.
observations.label: Violence and flight

observations.body: At a well in Midian, Moses helps Reuel’s daughters, remains with their household, and names his son for life as a foreigner.
observations.label: A foreign land

observations.body: The king dies, but the children of Israel remain in bondage and their cry rises to God.
observations.label: Many days

observations.body: The closing lines say that God heard, remembered, saw, and understood.
observations.label: Four divine verbs

payload.posture: Keep Moses’ movement in Midian and Israel’s bondage in Egypt together without merging their actions.
payload.tension: Moses settles as a foreigner in Midian while Israel’s cry continues to rise from bondage in Egypt.
payload.title: Flight, waiting, and a cry heard
